hints: Sketch both molecules in your head from glycerol outwards. How many fatty acids and what else is attached in a phospholipid versus a triglyceride?
Remember an ester bond forms every time a fatty acid (or phosphate) joins to glycerol by condensation. Count those joins for each molecule.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two structures**

Both molecules are built on one glycerol backbone. That is your starting point.

A triglyceride has three fatty acids attached to that glycerol. A phospholipid has only two fatty acids plus one phosphate group attached.

**Count the ester bonds**

Each condensation between glycerol and a fatty acid makes one ester bond.

So triglyceride makes 3 ester bonds, while phospholipid makes only 2 ester bonds to its fatty acids.

**Pick the correct comparison**

That means the phospholipid has fewer ester bonds and the triglyceride has more ester bonds. This matches row C exactly.

options.A: The phosphate head is hydrophilic, not hydrophobic. It loves water, which is why phospholipids can face water in membranes.
options.B: Both molecules contain only one glycerol molecule. A triglyceride has one glycerol plus three fatty acids, not three glycerols.
options.C: Correct. A phospholipid has 2 fatty acid ester bonds while a triglyceride has 3, so the phospholipid has fewer and the triglyceride has more.
options.D: This is back to front. A phospholipid has fewer fatty acids (2) and a triglyceride has more (3).
